correctness.rationale: The proof establishes equivalence of positive constant powers with a unique rooted functional digraph, the exact total \(f^fN^m\), Cayley count \(f^{f-1}\) on the fixed sector, and a weighted Prüfer enumeration \(fN^{m-1}\) for \(m\geq1\). The \(f=0\) and \(m=0\) boundaries and \(n=1\) exception are explicit. The pairmorph bijection and composition of magma powers are checked directly. Exhaustive code tests all \(n\leq3\) magma operation tables and nine small equivariance types; finite checks support rather than replace universal proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Baiduk–Kozerenko Theorem 3 proves the transformation representation, an ingredient but not the number of functional digraphs with one attracting root. Its idempotent and regular enumerations count different predicates. López-Permouth enumerates idempotents only. Owusu-Mensah's Proposition 8 shows some commutative constant-diagonal operations have constant squares, a restricted class with no complete all-n count. Konieczny's full paper proves Green relation / regularity theorems and induced permutation-orbit maps, none stated as eventual-constant numerical counts. Combining known orbit parametrization with the weighted rooted-forest proof is genuinely required.

Another formulation is the size of the union of cyclic-power classes of all constant magma operations. The pairmorph isomorphism is already known and not claimed new; its existing theorems determine ideals, idempotents and regularity, whereas the new statement requires acyclic free-orbit forests and an explicit total. The small-power examples of the generator paper do not determine that total.

originality.rationale: Closest complete source (arxiv:2607.13746) identifies pairmorph transformations but its results enumerate ideals, idempotents and regular operations, not eventual constant powers. Primary comparisons with López-Permouth and Owusu-Mensah show no all-n count or arbitrary-involution neutrality theorem. Broad semantic record checks produced no equivalent claim; a stronger unidentified general centralizer theorem could still imply the formula, so the historical risk is explicitly retained rather than ruled out.
residual_risks: An earlier general enumeration of equivariant rooted forests or permutation centralizer constant-power classes, outside the primary texts inspected, might imply the formula under different terminology.
The pairmorph isomorphism, induced permutation-orbit map, and Prüfer counting identity are established prior mathematics and are not claimed independently new.
Semantic searches and full-text comparisons cannot certify exhaustive worldwide historical priority.

value.rationale: A global power-defined subset of the finite magma monoid has the unexpectedly simple exact density \(1/n^2\). More fundamentally, the density \(1/N\) is invariant under restricting all transformations to the centralizer of any involution with at least one fixed point, even though that restriction drastically changes the sample space. The result is a complete all-dimensional classification for a natural semigroup-theoretic statistic, with a structural weighted-tree mechanism and explicit fixed-point-free boundary; it is not a routine finite case or an arbitrary slice.
